newsitem.title: USA: CIA spent $100 million on anti-Saddam effort - Post.
newsitem.headline: CIA spent $100 million on anti-Saddam effort - Post.

text.p: The Central Intelligence Agency spent about $100 million since 1991 to implement a classified 1991 presidential order to oust Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, the Washington Post reported in Sunday editions.

The paper quoted administration, congressional and dissident Iraqi sources as saying that despite the money spent on the anti-Saddam campaign, the U.S. spy agency had very little to show for its effort.

The Post said the CIA had funded dissident Kurds and Iraqis, enabling them to buy light arms and ammunition, communications gear, publishing materials, broadcasting equipment, cars and trucks, food and medicine.
The CIA's operation in northern Iraq fell apart last month when Massoud Barzani, a Kurdish rebel leader, requested Saddam's military assistance to oust a rival Kurdish group from the region.

Barzani's rebels of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) are virtually in control of most of northern Iraq after routing rivals of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) headed by Jalal Talabani in less than two weeks of clashes.
